title: Lyra Biotech — budget vs latency tradeoffs POC scoping
summary: POC scoping to align on unit economics targets, benchmark plan, workload sizing and 6-week timeline. Customer cares about per-token cost under constrained budget, sub-200ms p95 generation latency for 512-token workloads, and clear gating criteria for dedicated capacity. Next steps include Redwood sending a tailored cost model spreadsheet, Lyra to share representative dataset and QPS profile, and scheduling the benchmark run next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Samir (CSM) — Dr. Priya Rao (Lyra Head of Platform), Jonas Park (ML Eng Lead), Tanya Ruiz (SRE), Marco Li (Product)

Summary (auto): align on cost targets, define benchmark workload, agree timeline and decision gate for Dedicated vs Hosted.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, I'll lead the commercial side, Ethan is the SE who will run the bench. Samir is on for success ops. Priya, do you want to kick off with context?
[00:18] Dr. Priya Rao (Lyra): Sure yeah, hi. We're a computational biology shop, lots of sequence-to-structure inference, LLMs used in internal assistants and retrieval-augmented generation. Main driver here is cost predictability — we have a strict monthly budget for API spend and we need p95 latency guarantees for dev and prod.
[00:35] Jonas Park (ML Eng): Also, our median generation is roughly 320 tokens but the 95th is around 900, so tail matters. We do a mix of short QA and long summarization.
[00:50] Ethan (Redwood SE): Great, that's helpful. For cost modeling we usually break down by workload class — short generation, long generation, and embeddings/ranking. Could you share QPS and concurrency targets?
[01:05] Jonas: For POC we want to simulate peak: 35 QPS across a pool with bursts to 120 concurrent infer requests, sustained for a few minutes. Typical daily sustained is 6 QPS.
[01:20] Maya: Budget front — what's the monthly cap you're trying to model against?
[01:25] Dr. Priya: We have an internal budget slice of $12k/month for model inference during evaluation phase; if Dedicated looks good we can expand. So rough per-token targets need to keep within that envelope.
[01:38] Marco Li (Product): And a gating condition: if we can't hit p95 < 200ms for typical 512 token gen at cost X we won't move to Dedicated.
[01:50] Ethan: Okay, couple of clarifications: p95 < 200ms for 512 tokens is aggressive; it depends on model family and quantization. Are you fixed on a specific model?
[02:05] Jonas: We're experimenting with an open-weights LLaMA-variant 30B and a distilled 7B for lower latency. Curious about quantized int8/4 profiles and what Redwood's runtime sees on 80GB A100 versus T4-like instances.
[02:22] Ethan: Right. Our cost model will show per-token CPU/GPU execution cost plus amortized infra. We can simulate two configs: hosted with automatic bursting and Dedicated reserved GPUs. For the same model, dedicated capacity reduces unit cost at scale due to packing and persistent KV cache.
[02:40] Dr. Priya: Can you explain the KV/prefix cache impact? We don't fully understand how much of our tokens will be saved.
[02:48] Ethan: Sure. If you have repeated prefixes — for example, standard system prompts or common retrieval contexts — Redwood's KV cache avoids re-computing attention keys for that prefix. Practically, for RAG setups with a 256 token retrieval context and repeated system prompt we often see 10-30% token-cost reduction for generation. But it depends on your query diversity.
[03:10] Jonas: Our retrieval context often includes 3 docs ~150 tokens each plus a 50 token system prompt, so there's some prefix repeat but not huge. Expect maybe 12-18% saving if caching aligns.
[03:24] Tanya: For Dedicated, what's the onboarding friction? We have strict network policies.
[03:30] Maya: Private/Dedicated requires VPC peering or Private Link and a short onboarding checklist — certs, SSO config, KMS integration if you want customer-managed keys. Typically 2-3 weeks to get a pilot environment if networking is straightforward.
[03:46] Samir (CSM): We'll provide a checklist after this call.
[03:50] [short crosstalk]
[04:05] Jonas: On benchmarks — Ethan, what's the recommended harness? We want to measure p50/p95/p99 for both latency and token throughput, and get per-token cost numbers.
[04:15] Ethan: We use a load harness that replays traces with real token distributions and supports variable batching windows, auto-prefix caching toggles, and quantization flags. We'll run each gen workload at increasing concurrency to find the knee of the curve. We'll export CSVs with request-level latency, tokens generated, and cost attribution per request.
[04:36] Maya: We'll also provide a cost spreadsheet — two scenarios: hosted consumption vs 3-month reserved Dedicated commit. That will let you see unit economics at your scale.
[04:45] Marco: Can you give a back-of-the-envelope per-token number for the 7B quantized case on Dedicated vs hosted? Even a ballpark helps.
[04:55] Ethan: Ballpark, assuming int8 quantization on 7B: hosted might be around $0.60–$1.20 per 1k generation tokens depending on batching and cache hit rate; Dedicated can drop to $0.20–$0.45 per 1k at sustained utilization and with efficient packing. These are rough — we'll put precise numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:20] Dr. Priya: That spread is big. Under our $12k/month cap, what sustained QPS does that imply?
[05:28] Ethan: Quick calc: at $0.5/1k tokens, $12k covers ~24M tokens/month. If median session is 320 tokens, that's ~75k sessions/month. But again, with dedicated and caching that token budget stretches further.
[05:48] Jonas: We need to include embedding costs — our vector DB upserts and retrieval pipelines also hit cost. How do you attribute those?
[05:58] Maya: Embeddings are separate unit economics; we'll include embeddings per-1k token (or per-vector) estimates. For the POC we'll model a combined cost line item.
[06:08] Tanya: Security question — do you have SOC2 reports and do logs leave our VPC on Dedicated?
[06:15] Maya: Yes SOC2 Type II, and with Dedicated/Private you can configure audit logs to stay in your account and use your KMS. We'll share the security packet.
[06:22] [00:07:00 marker — paraphrase of technical dive]
[07:00] Ethan: For the benchmark plan I propose three phases: 1) Baseline hosted run with your traces, 2) Dedicated pilot with identical harness, 3) Stress testing with synthetic worst-case sequences (long 900 token summaries). We'll measure cost, p95, and throughput.
[07:20] Jonas: Sounds good. How long does each run take?
[07:25] Ethan: Each workload sweep is about 1-2 hours to get stable stats; end-to-end for all phases maybe 6 hours over 2 days. We can do it in a scheduled window so it doesn't interfere with your dev traffic.
[07:40] Marco: We also want an A/B on quantization: int8 vs int4 for the 7B to see quality drop.
[07:47] Ethan: Yes we'll include that. Quick note on latency numbers: int4 may reduce memory and slightly speed things but can increase inference compute, it's model-dependent. We'll surface quality delta by running your reference eval prompts.
[08:02] Dr. Priya: Acceptance criteria recap: p95 < 200ms for 512 token typical gen OR per-token cost under $0.6/1k tokens with acceptable quality, AND embeddings within budget. If we hit these we consider Dedicated pilot.
[08:20] Maya: We'll convert that to a formal gating doc and share.
[08:25] [pause / background noise]
[09:00] Jonas: One more on batching knobs — can Redwood do aggressive dynamic batching for short queries while preserving low tail latency?
[09:10] Ethan: Yes, our runtime supports adaptive batching windows and latency SLO-driven batching. We can set max batch latency like 8ms and cap batch size so tails don't blow up. For Dedicated you can tune packing policies further.
[09:28] Tanya: Any pre-warm strategies? For example, keep-hot KV caches for common prompts?
[09:33] Ethan: You can pin hot prefixes or keep a warmed pool of workers; that helps for predictable patterns. But it costs reserved capacity. We'll model that tradeoff.
[09:45] Maya: Ok, timeline proposal: week 1 (this week) — share cost spreadsheet and traces; week 2 — benchmark hosted; week 3 — spin up Dedicated pilot if gating looks promising; week 4–6 — iterate and measure, then decision at end of week 6. Does that align?
[10:02] Dr. Priya: Yes sounds reasonable. We may accelerate network approvals to get Dedicated sooner.
[10:10] Marco: Can you send sample CSV headers for the traces we should upload?
[10:15] Ethan: I'll attach the trace schema: timestamp, request_id, prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, model_hint, user_id_hash. Jonas, will that work?
[10:26] Jonas: Yep, we'll produce that.
[10:30] [11:00 marker — run-through of potential objections]
[11:00] Jonas: A common concern from infra is that Dedicated lock-in increases ops overhead. What's rollback look like if costs spike?
[11:08] Maya: We'll add fallback policies — Redwood can route to hosted for overflow, and you can set budget alarms and auto-fallback in the Console. Dedicated commit can also include burst to hosted.
[11:20] Tanya: For compliance, can we keep request logs for only 30 days? We have retention limits.
[11:27] Samir: Yes, retention is configurable; we'll note it in the security packet.
[11:32] [Minor transcription glitch here — "Kanji" appears where KMS was meant] 
[11:50] Ethan: For the benchmark we'll produce CSVs and also a small dashboard with per-route token cost and lat buckets so you can quickly see where cost is concentrated.
[12:02] Dr. Priya: Great. One more ask — can you show a sensitivity analysis: how cost changes if cache hit rate is 0%, 15%, 30%?
[12:12] Maya: Absolutely. We'll include a sensitivity table in the spreadsheet and a chart.
[12:20] Jonas: Regarding concurrency patterns, our traces show spikes every 10 minutes for batch jobs — can the harness reproduce that?
[12:28] Ethan: Yes, we'll replay the trace and also add synthetic spike patterns.
[12:34] [Wrap-up segment]
[12:40] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send cost model + security docs + trace schema; Lyra to send traces and approve a 2-hour benchmark window next week; Redwood to run hosted benchmark and then spin up Dedicated pilot if gating met. We will set a decision checkpoint end of week 6.
[12:58] Dr. Priya: Thank you — appreciate the clarity.
[13:05] Jonas: Quick note — include embedding unit costs and an example of how retrieval cache affects end-to-end latency for RAG.
[13:12] Ethan: Noted.
[13:20] Maya: Any last blockers? If not we'll close and follow up with calendar invites and the doc bundle.
[13:28] Tanya: No blockers. Thanks.
[13:32] Maya: Great thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Bench plan attachment references: Redwood cost spreadsheet (link sent after call), benchmark harness repo (github.com/redwood/bench-harness — reference), security packet (link to S3 / internal share).
